title: HomeGuard Homeowners Policy Estimating Standard — Access Tear-Out to Reach a Frozen Supply Line
content:
**Standard.** On the dwelling water damage of a HomeGuard Homeowners Policy claim settled in place of a repeated-seepage denial, an access tear-out allowance for opening walls, floors or ceilings to reach a frozen supply line is added at a percentage of the replacement-cost value: 6 percent for a freeze loss whose dwelling water damage has a replacement-cost value of at least 10000.00, 3 percent for a freeze loss below that value, and none for a sudden discharge, whose tear-out of the wet materials around the discharge point is already inside the replacement-cost value of the damage, while a frozen line runs inside exterior walls beyond the wet area.

The allowance is added to the reversal payment on the dwelling water damage before the floor at 0.00 and the single rounding to the cent.

## Questions the standard answers

**Which cause of loss earns the allowance?**
A freeze, as recorded on the claim's first notice. A sudden and accidental discharge of water earns none.

**Which replacement-cost value decides between 6 and 3 percent, and which value is the percentage taken on?**
The replacement-cost value of the dwelling water damage recorded on its repeated-seepage denial entry, in both cases.

**What happens exactly at 10000.00?**
A freeze loss at exactly 10000.00 is "at least 10000.00" and takes 6 percent. At 9999.99 it takes 3 percent.

**Why is a sudden discharge treated differently?**
The tear-out around a discharge point is already inside the replacement-cost value of the damage, while a frozen line runs inside exterior walls beyond the wet area.

## Decision table

| Cause of loss | Replacement-cost value of the dwelling water damage | Allowance |
|---|---|---|
| freeze | 10000.00 or more | 6 percent |
| freeze | below 10000.00 | 3 percent |
| sudden and accidental discharge | any | none |

**Hypothetical figures.** A freeze loss valued at 12000.00 adds 720.00; a freeze loss valued at 8000.00 adds 240.00; a sudden-discharge loss valued at 12000.00 adds nothing.
